column1: # What an attacker controls, where the webhook schema cannot tell: a path
# below github.event (** is any number of segments), or a name below github
# other than event; its capability (fixed, login-prefixed, named, repo-name, dashed, structured,
# commit-email, page-name, hyphenless, arbitrary: named is structured that holds no [ and does
# not begin with :, such as the name of a ref, a repository or a label
# (owner:branch); login-prefixed is named that begins with the login of an
# account, so that it does not begin with -, a path below github.event only,
# such as a label or the full name of a repository (owner/name); repo-name is named that may begin with - and holds only
# ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, the name of a repository; dashed is
# named that may begin with - and holds other characters too, such as the
# name of a pull request's head branch; commit-email is structured where an attacker writes a
# workflow command of the runner, the email of a git commit; page-name is
# structured that may begin with -, holds no blank or line break, and where
# an attacker writes add-path but no workflow command that takes a property
# (set-env, set-output), the name of a wiki page; hyphenless is
# arbitrary that holds no - of ASCII, so that no workflow command whose name
# has a - is in it, the title of a wiki page); why; and, if any, events: for a name below
# github, the events that set it (in the others it is absent); for a path
# below github.event, the events whose tables the line is for (in the
# others the path keeps what the schema gives).
# In a path below github.event, {a,b} stands for the path with each choice
# in its place; a choice may hold dots.
# Every line must match, and every choice of its braces, in each of its
# events; tablegen stops on one that matches nothing.
